title: `name_index` takes 0.8 s on 2.4M fasta records, all on one thread
body:
`name_index()` on a mapped `Framed` (`index.rs`, `Framed::name_index`) gives the index its names. It passes a closure to `Index::name_with`, and the closure reads each record's bytes through `Source::range` and finds the name with `seq::name_of`. `name_with` then does three things, all on one thread:

- It takes each name as `Cow::Owned(name.to_vec())`, one allocation per record. The closure has to own the name because `name_with`'s closure type ties the returned `Cow` to the `&Offset` and not to the source, so a slice borrowed from the map cannot be returned.
- It copies each name onto `blob`, one concatenated `Vec<u8>`, and records a start and length per record in `spans`.
- It fills `by_name` with every named record's position as a `u32`, then stable-sorts it with `sort_by`. Each comparison looks both names up in `blob`.

nail measured it while timing its own input indexing. On a fasta of 2,455,940 MGnify records, about 535 MB, with a warm page cache on a 16-core x86_64 box:

| step | seconds |
|---|---|
| `Framed::map` | 0.07 |
| `Framed::map`, then `name_index()` | 0.87 to 0.94 |

So naming costs about 0.8 s. Nobody has measured how that splits between the copies and the sort. A sort of 2.4M entries makes about 50M comparisons, and each one reads two names at scattered places in `blob`. That pattern likely misses the cache. In nail, a binary search per record over the same `by_name` cost about 950 ns per record for the same reason. The sort is the likely main cost, though that has not been checked. At the MGnify scale of about 2.456 billion records, the same cost would be on the order of 800 s if it scales linearly. Nobody has measured that either.

nail calls `Index::name` for its output and no longer calls `Index::position`, so nothing in nail reads `by_name` today.

## Proposal

Measure the split first, then choose among these:

| option | what changes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| A. borrow from the source | `name_with`'s closure may return a name borrowed from the source, so a mapped source copies each name once, into `blob` | a changed signature on public `Index::name_with`, which is breaking |
| B. parallel sort | `par_sort_by` in place of `sort_by`; rayon's version is stable, so `position` keeps answering with the first of a repeated name | `rayon` as a `libsail` dependency, or behind a feature |
| C. names without the order | a way to build `blob` and `spans` without `by_name`, for a caller that only reads names | a new public method, and an index whose `position` cannot answer |

## Open

- C conflicts with option C of sail-c04fbf, which reports repeated names from `by_name` and so needs the sort on every naming. If that decision lands on reporting, the sort is no longer optional, and B is the option that helps.
- Whether the `Source::range` scan, done one record at a time, costs anything worth measuring next to the sort.
close_reason: Landed in 9b3d591 on dev. The sort orders (Span, position) pairs, and Span packs into one NonZeroU64. The measurements and the reasons A, B and C were dropped are in the note.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/424f83e5
notes.text:
Measured on a synthetic FASTA of 2,455,940 records named like `MGYP000001234567`, with a warm page cache, on one thread. The sort was most of the cost, and the file's order decided how much. `name_index` took 0.065 s when the names were already in order and 0.83 s when they were shuffled. The scan and copy took 0.06 s either way.

The sort was slow because each comparison reached a name through two dependent reads, first from `by_name` into `spans` and then into `blob`. Each entry of `spans` was a 24-byte `Option<Span>`. Sorting `(Span, position)` pairs reaches `blob` in one read, and took 0.23 s where the old sort took 0.70 s. `sort_unstable_by` with the position as the tie-break gives the same order the stable sort gave.

Decided with Jack:

- A is dropped. The scan and copy cost at most 0.066 s, so borrowing from the source saves little. The copy it would have removed is gone anyway: `name_index` and `build_named` now push borrowed names into a private `NameBuilder` and no longer go through `name_with`.
- B is dropped. Jack does not want `rayon` in `libsail`.
- C is dropped. The index file stores `by_name` and `position` needs it, so every naming sorts.
- Memory matters as much as speed. `Span` is now one `NonZeroU64` holding the start and the length, so an `Option<Span>` takes 8 bytes where it took 24. The pairs cost 16 bytes per named record while the sort runs. The peak while naming stays where it was, and the finished index is smaller.

Before and after, on the same file:

| run | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `name_index` on a mapped file, shuffled names | 0.94 to 1.19 s | 0.26 s |
| `name_index` on a mapped file, names in order | 0.07 s | 0.05 s |
| `build_named`, shuffled names | 0.98 s, 274 MB peak | 0.31 s, 150 MB peak |
| `build_named`, names in order | 0.17 s, 274 MB peak | 0.11 s, 150 MB peak |
